name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian
    Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to
    families with dependent children. The considered scenario focuses exclusively
    on applications submitted directly by interested users through the INPS website,
    excluding applications submitted by delegated patronage institutions, mobile
    applications, and call-center interactions.

    An authenticated applicant can submit an AUU application as a parent,
    foster parent, or legal guardian of a child. During the first phase of the
    application, the applicant provides information about each dependent child,
    including the child's fiscal code, dependency status, disability status and,
    when applicable, disability level. Depending on the applicant type, additional
    information concerning family composition, exclusive custody, the other
    parent's fiscal code, and the requested allowance distribution between parents
    must also be provided.

    When a child's fiscal code is entered, the system verifies it in real time.
    If the child is already associated with another active application, the
    application flow is blocked and an explanatory warning is shown. The applicant
    may also specify adult dependent children who do not directly qualify for AUU
    but contribute to determining household composition. Duplicate fiscal codes for
    adult children are detected and reported.

    The amount of the allowance depends on the applicant's economic situation.
    If INPS does not already possess a valid ISEE when the application is submitted,
    the minimum allowance established by regulation is used. If a valid ISEE becomes
    available later, INPS automatically recalculates the allowance without requiring
    the applicant to modify the application.

    In the payment phase, the applicant specifies the payment method. If the
    allowance is to be divided equally between both parents, the payment information
    of the other parent must also be provided. Supported payment methods include
    credit to a SEPA IBAN account owned by the beneficiary, domiciled payment at a
    post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card.

    Before submitting the application, the applicant must read and accept the
    declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice. The system then
    presents a summary of the entered information so that it can be reviewed.
    If validation errors are detected, the application is not submitted and the
    applicant must correct the erroneous information. If validation succeeds, the
    application is submitted and a receipt can be downloaded.

    An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before
    submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed. When resuming
    a draft, the applicant may either continue from the previously saved information
    or discard it and restart the application from the beginning.

    Once submitted, the application is evaluated by authorized INPS staff.
    The application may be accepted, rejected because the applicant is not entitled
    to the benefit, or suspended when additional documentation is required.
    The applicant is notified of the outcome. An accepted application remains valid
    for twelve months and the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every
    month.

    When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional
    documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the
    requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the
    responsibility declarations and privacy notice.

    The system also allows an application originally submitted by one parent to be
    completed by the other parent. The other parent can consult the application and
    confirm or modify the proposed allowance distribution. If the applicant requested
    the entire allowance, the other parent may accept the 100 percent allocation or
    request a 50 percent distribution. When payment to the other parent is required,
    that parent provides their own payment information.

    Applicants can also add one or more children to an existing application.
    Each new child's fiscal code is checked in real time to ensure that the child
    is not already associated with another active application. After adding the
    child, existing payment and declaration data can be confirmed or modified.

    Finally, the system provides supporting functions that allow citizens to consult
    previously submitted applications, consult general information about the
    Assegno Unico Universale, and simulate the expected monthly allowance amount.

highLevelGoals: To successfully submit a new application for the Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) benefit, providing all necessary personal and child-related information.
To save an incomplete application as a draft and later resume or discard it, allowing for flexible completion of the application process.
To provide and manage the preferred method and details for receiving the AUU allowance.
To track the progress and outcome (accepted, rejected, suspended) of submitted AUU applications.
To upload additional documents and reconfirm application data when an application is suspended by INPS staff.
To update or add information, such as new children, to an already submitted and active AUU application.
To consult general information about the AUU benefit and simulate potential allowance amounts.
To acknowledge and accept the responsibility declarations and GDPR privacy notice required for application submission.
To obtain a downloadable receipt as confirmation of successful application submission.
To receive timely notification regarding the final decision (accepted, rejected, or suspended) of a submitted AUU application.
To ensure that all dependent child and adult dependent fiscal codes are valid and unique, preventing duplicate entries or applications.
To access and review all previously submitted AUU applications, including their complete history and details, beyond just current status.
To access an AUU application initiated by the other parent and provide necessary information to finalize it.
To review, confirm, or modify the proposed distribution of the AUU allowance between both parents and specify personal payment information for their share.
To review, evaluate, and make a decision (accept, reject, or suspend) on submitted AUU applications, including requesting additional documentation when necessary.
To ensure the AUU allowance is automatically recalculated and updated when a valid ISEE becomes available, reflecting the correct economic situation without requiring applicant intervention.
To ensure the approved AUU allowance is automatically disbursed to beneficiaries on a monthly basis for the duration of the application's validity.

The system must verify that the submitted dependent fiscal code adheres to the predefined national format rules (e.g., length, character set, checksum). This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/fiscal-codes/validate-format?code={fiscalCode}.

The system must check if a submitted dependent fiscal code already exists among other dependents within the Applicant's current application. This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/applications/{applicationId}/dependents/check-uniqueness?code={fiscalCode}.

The system must verify that a submitted dependent fiscal code is not already associated with an active, approved application by any other applicant in the entire system. This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/dependents/check-global-uniqueness?code={fiscalCode}.

The system must query an external authoritative registry (e.g., national tax agency, civil registry) to fetch official demographic and status details for a validated dependent fiscal code. This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/external-registry/dependent-details?fiscalCode={fiscalCode}.

The system must persist the successfully validated and enriched dependent fiscal code and associated official data into the Applicant's application record. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/dependents with the dependent data.

The system must provide clear and specific feedback to the Applicant, indicating success or detailing any validation errors (e.g., invalid format, duplicate within application, globally duplicate). This feedback would be part of the response from an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/dependents.

The system must allow the Applicant to save the current state of an application as a draft, enabling them to resume editing later. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/draft.

The system must enable the Applicant to select a preferred payment method (e.g., bank transfer, postal order) and capture the required payment details (e.g., IBAN, account holder name). This could be implemented via an API call like PUT /api/applications/{applicationId}/payment-method.

The system must record the Applicant's acceptance of mandatory declarations and terms of service before final submission. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/declarations/accept.

The system must generate and provide a downloadable receipt or confirmation document after a successful application submission. This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/applications/{applicationId}/receipt/download.

The system must permit the Applicant to upload additional supporting documents (e.g., proof of income, disability certificates) when an application is suspended or requires further evidence. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/documents/upload.

The system must allow the Applicant to invite the other parent to complete their portion of a joint application, typically by sending a secure link or notification. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/invite-other-parent.

The system must allow the Applicant to add a new dependent child record to their application, initiating the data entry and validation process for that child. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/{applicationId}/dependents/add-child.

The system must enable the Applicant to view a list of their previously submitted or drafted applications, including their current status. This could be implemented via an API call like GET /api/applicants/{applicantId}/applications.

The system must allow the Applicant to input preliminary data and receive an estimated calculation of the potential Assegno Unico Universale benefit amount. This could be implemented via an API call like POST /api/applications/simulate-allowance.

The system shall allow the applicant to fetch a paginated list of all their previously submitted Assegno Unico Universale (AUU) applications, including basic identifying information like application ID, submission date, and current status.

The system shall allow the applicant to select a specific application from their list and retrieve all its associated data, such as applicant details, beneficiary information, requested amounts, and attached documents.

The system shall allow the applicant to view a chronological log of all status transitions and significant events related to a specific AUU application, including timestamps and descriptions of each change.

The system shall allow the applicant to filter their list of submitted AUU applications based on criteria such as application status (e.g., 'approved', 'pending', 'rejected'), submission year, or specific keywords within the application details.

INPS Staff retrieves the status of the latest ISEE data ingestion process for a specific applicant, confirming if new data was successfully processed.
INPS Staff retrieves and reviews the outcome of an automatically triggered AUU allowance recalculation for a specific applicant, including the proposed new amount.
INPS Staff explicitly triggers the system to recalculate the AUU allowance for an applicant, overriding or re-running an automatic process if needed.
INPS Staff reviews the proposed new AUU allowance amount (resulting from an automatic or manual recalculation) and explicitly approves its update to the applicant's official record.
INPS Staff queries and views the detailed audit trail of an AUU allowance adjustment for a specific applicant, including old/new values, triggers (automatic/manual), and timestamps.
INPS Staff accesses and examines the current set of AUU allowance calculation rules and parameters used by the system for automatic adjustments.
INPS Staff reviews the content of an automated notification generated for an allowance adjustment for a specific applicant before or after its dispatch.
Applicant sends a request to the system to begin a new AUU allowance application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to save the current state of their in-progress AUU allowance application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to add or update the details of a dependent child within their application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to upload a specific supporting document file for their application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to confirm their acceptance of all mandatory declarations and terms for the AUU allowance.
Applicant sends a request to the system to select or modify their preferred payment method for receiving the AUU allowance.
Applicant sends a request to the system to formally submit their finalized AUU allowance application for processing.
Applicant sends a request to the system to retrieve and display the current processing status of their submitted AUU allowance application.
Applicant sends a request to the system to retrieve and display the details of any recent adjustments made to their AUU allowance.
Applicant sends a request to the system to update their personal contact information (e.g., address, phone, email) associated with their profile.
The system shall query the application database to retrieve all approved AUU applications that are active and have a scheduled disbursement date for the current month.
For each identified eligible application, the system shall fetch the associated beneficiary's approved allowance amount and registered payment method details.
The system shall send a request to the external financial system to initiate a payment transaction for the specified allowance amount to the beneficiary's registered payment account.

Upon successful initiation or completion of a payment transaction, the system shall update the corresponding application's disbursement history with the payment date, amount, status, and set the next scheduled disbursement date.
Before initiating a payment, the system shall verify that the current disbursement falls within the approved validity period of the application.
After the final valid monthly disbursement has been successfully processed for an application, the system shall update the application's overall status to 'Expired'.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to initiate a new AUU application and save its initial state as a draft.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to save the current progress of an in-progress AUU application as a draft.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to retrieve and continue editing a previously saved AUU application draft.
The system shall validate the entered child fiscal code against the national registry in real-time and display a warning if it is already linked to another active application.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to input and update details for each child associated with the AUU application.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to input and update family composition details relevant to the AUU application.
The system shall record the applicant's explicit acceptance of the responsibility declarations required for the AUU application submission.
The system shall record the applicant's explicit acceptance of the GDPR privacy notice.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to select a preferred payment method from a predefined list for allowance disbursement.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to confirm the selected payment method details for allowance disbursement.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to upload required additional documentation for a suspended AUU application.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to add details for a new child to an already submitted and active AUU application.
The system shall allow an authenticated applicant to view the status and details of their submitted AUU applications.
The system shall provide a tool for an authenticated applicant to simulate the potential AUU allowance amount based on entered family and income data.
The system shall allow INPS staff to access and review all submitted application details and supporting documentation for evaluation.
The system shall allow INPS staff to mark an application as 'Approved' after successful evaluation, triggering initial allowance calculation.
The system shall allow INPS staff to mark an application as 'Rejected', providing a reason for the rejection.
The system shall allow INPS staff to mark an application as 'Suspended', requesting additional documentation from the applicant.
The system shall allow INPS staff to specify and request particular additional documentation from an applicant for a suspended application.

baselineCritiques.highLevelGoals: The list captures most of the functional intentions described, but there are a few issues. The goals “Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE” and “Ensure Timely Allowance Disbursement” describe system‑driven behavior rather than an explicit user‑oriented purpose; they belong to low‑level/technical goals and are incorrectly assigned to INPS staff. Additionally, the “Process and Decide on AUU Applications” goal could be split to explicitly include “Notify applicant of decision” which is only implied elsewhere. Overall the set is fairly complete, but the mis‑placement of automatic system actions lowers the score.
baselineCritiques.lowLevelGoals:
[Applicant -> Submit AUU Application] The low‑level goals are largely well‑aligned with the described user actions and are all functional. They cover initiating, drafting, editing, validating, and submitting an application, as well as handling second‑parent participation, document upload, payment details, and simulation. However, the set omits a key applicant action described in the specification: after the INPS staff evaluate the application, the applicant must be able to view the outcome (accepted, rejected, or suspended) and any associated decision document or notification. Adding low‑level goals such as “The system shall allow the Applicant to view the current status and decision of a submitted application” and “The system shall allow the Applicant to download the decision letter or notification” would make the list complete.

[Applicant -> Manage Application Drafts] The low‑level goals are all functional, each describes a single action the Applicant can perform on application drafts, and they map cleanly to the sole high‑level goal “Manage Application Drafts”. There are no non‑functional statements, contradictions, or missing actions for the draft‑management scope (create, update, list, load, delete). The set is complete for the defined high‑level goal.

[Applicant -> Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup] The low‑level goal set is far from complete and is incorrectly structured. All goals are linked to a single high‑level goal (“Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup”) even though many of them belong to other strategic objectives such as “Create and Manage AUU Application”, “Handle Supporting Documents”, “View Application Status”, “Simulate Allowance”, and “Co‑parent Collaboration”. Important functional actions described in the system narrative are missing, e.g.:

* Real‑time fiscal‑code validation that blocks duplicate active applications.  
* Adding adult dependent children and detecting duplicate adult fiscal codes.  
* Automatic recalculation of the allowance when a valid ISEE becomes available.  
* Receiving outcome notifications (accepted, rejected, suspended) and viewing the decision.  
* Uploading additional documents after a suspension and resubmitting.  
* Co‑parent actions: consulting the partner’s application, confirming/modifying allowance distribution, providing their own payment details, and accepting a 50 % split when the other parent requested 100 %.  
* Discarding a draft and restarting the application from scratch.  
* Consulting general information about AUU and running an allowance simulation.  

Conversely, the current list contains many goals that are unrelated to payment setup (e.g., “InitiateNewAUUApplication”, “AddChildDataToApplication”, “RequestAllowanceSimulation”) and therefore should be associated with appropriate high‑level goals.  

To improve the model you should:

1. Define additional high‑level goals that reflect the major business concerns (application creation, validation, draft management, outcome handling, co‑parent collaboration, allowance simulation, etc.).  
2. Re‑assign each low‑level goal to the correct high‑level goal.  
3. Add missing low‑level goals for the functionalities listed above.  
4. Remove any duplicated or irrelevant goals and ensure each low‑level goal describes a single functional action of the applicant.

[Applicant -> Monitor Application Status] The low‑level goals contain several serious issues. First, they reference many high‑level goals (e.g., Create Application, Manage Application Data, Handle Payments, Submit Application, Simulate Allowance, Provide Informational Services, Collaborate on Application) that are not present in the high‑level goal list, creating a mismatch between the two layers. Second, the actor model is incomplete: the low‑level goals introduce a “Co‑Applicant/Other Parent” actor, yet the actors section defines only a single “Applicant” actor, leading to an inconsistency. Third, while most goals are functional, some are redundant or overly granular (e.g., separate goals for “RetrieveSubmittedApplicationsSummary” and “GetApplicationCurrentStatus” could be merged). Finally, the low‑level goal set does not fully cover all functional aspects described (e.g., real‑time fiscal‑code validation during child addition, draft‑resume options, notification of status changes) in a clear one‑action‑per‑goal format. Overall, the low‑level goals are inconsistent with the defined high‑level goals and actor model, and they miss alignment with the system description.

[Applicant -> Respond to Documentation Requests] The low‑level goals are all functional and each maps to a concrete action an Applicant can perform to satisfy the high‑level goal “Respond to Documentation Requests”. They cover retrieving suspended applications, getting details, uploading required documents, updating requested data fields, and resubmitting the application for review. No non‑functional or unrelated goals are present, and there are no contradictions with the description. The set could be slightly enriched by adding a goal to view the updated status or confirmation after resubmission, but overall the coverage is solid.

[Applicant -> Modify Existing Application] The low‑level goals are largely functional and map well to single actions an applicant can perform when modifying an existing AUU application. They cover selecting an application, retrieving details, adding/updating child data, validating fiscal codes, handling payment information for both parents, adjusting allowance distribution, uploading required documents, confirming suspension requirements, reviewing validation errors, re‑accepting declarations, saving/discarding drafts, reviewing a summary, submitting the modification and downloading a receipt.  

Minor issues:  
1. There is no explicit “Resume Draft” goal (e.g., load a saved draft for continuation), which is a distinct user action described in the system.  
2. A “Delete Child” action is not represented, though the description does not explicitly require it, it could be considered for completeness.  

Adding a low‑level goal such as “ResumeDraftApplication” would improve coverage.

[Applicant -> Access Benefit Information] The low‑level goals only address the “Access Benefit Information” high‑level goal (overview, eligibility criteria, simulation input and result). They completely ignore the core functional capabilities described in the system description, such as creating, saving, and submitting AUU applications; real‑time fiscal‑code validation; handling ISEE data; selecting and providing payment information; accepting declarations and privacy notices; generating receipts; managing drafts; supporting multi‑parent collaboration; adding children to an existing application; uploading supporting documents for suspended applications; and consulting previously submitted applications. Because the low‑level goals are far from comprehensive and omit essential user actions, the set is not representative of the software system.

[Applicant -> Accept Legal Declarations] The low‑level goal set is inconsistent with the high‑level model and the system description.  
* Only one high‑level goal (“Accept Legal Declarations”) is defined, yet the low‑level goals reference many other high‑level goals (e.g., Manage Child Information, Select Payment Method, Upload Supporting Documents, Review and Submit Application, Consult Past Applications, Run Allowance Simulations) that are missing from the high‑level list. This breaks the GORE traceability rule that each low‑level goal must be associated with an existing high‑level goal.  
* Several essential functional actions described in the specification are absent:  
  - Real‑time blocking of a child’s fiscal code when it is already linked to another active application (including duplicate adult‑child checks).  
  - Automatic recalculation of the allowance when a valid ISEE becomes available after submission.  
  - Notification of the applicant about the outcome of the evaluation (accepted, rejected, suspended).  
  - Download of the submission receipt.  
  - Ability for the other parent to complete or modify an already‑submitted application, including changing the allowance distribution and providing their own payment details.  
  - Uploading additional documents after a suspension and reconfirming the application.  
  - Access to general information about the AUU benefit.  
* Some low‑level goals are overly granular or duplicate functionality (e.g., separate “Retrieve” and “Display” actions for declarations) and could be merged for clarity.  
* All goals are functional, but the set is incomplete and misaligned with the defined high‑level goals.

To improve:  
1. Define the missing high‑level goals that reflect the major business objectives (e.g., “Manage Child Information”, “Select Payment Method”, “Submit Application”, “Handle Application Outcomes”, “Support Multi‑Parent Collaboration”, “Automatic Allowance Recalculation”, “Provide Benefit Information”).  
2. Align every low‑level goal with one of these high‑level goals.  
3. Add low‑level goals for the omitted functional actions listed above.  
4. Consolidate overly fine‑grained goals where appropriate.

[Applicant -> Receive Application Receipt] The low‑level goals focus exclusively on receipt handling and many of them describe system‑side behavior (e.g., “Generate Application Receipt”, “Store Application Receipt”, “Display Receipt Availability”) rather than a single action performed by the applicant. According to the GORE rules each low‑level goal should map to an actor’s concrete interaction with the software. Moreover, the only high‑level goal present is “Receive Application Receipt”, which ignores the majority of the functional scope described (application submission, draft saving, child addition, real‑time fiscal‑code validation, ISEE handling, payment method entry, declaration acceptance, document upload for suspended applications, multi‑parent collaboration, status consultation, simulation, etc.). Consequently, the low‑level goal set is both incomplete and mis‑aligned with the actors and the system description.

[Applicant -> Be Informed of Application Outcome] The three low‑level goals are all functional and directly support the single high‑level goal “Be Informed of Application Outcome.” They each describe a distinct interaction (querying status, receiving a status‑change alert, and reviewing past notifications). The only minor issue is that “ReceiveAutomatedStatusChangeNotification” describes a system‑initiated behavior rather than an explicit applicant action; phrasing it as “The applicant shall be able to receive …” would better align with the guideline that each goal corresponds to an actor’s action. Otherwise, the set is consistent and free of non‑functional or irrelevant items.

[Applicant -> Ensure Valid Child Data Submission] The low‑level goal set is poorly aligned with the sole high‑level goal (“Ensure Valid Child Data Submission”). While the first few goals correctly address fiscal‑code format, intra‑application uniqueness, global uniqueness, external data retrieval, storage, and feedback, the majority of the listed goals (draft handling, payment method selection, declaration acceptance, receipt generation, document upload, parent invitation, adding dependents, retrieving past applications, allowance simulation) address completely different concerns that are not covered by any high‑level goal. This violates the GORE principle that each low‑level goal should trace to a specific high‑level objective. Moreover, important functional actions described in the system narrative are missing, such as: real‑time blocking of the flow when a child is already linked to another active application, detection of duplicate adult‑dependent fiscal codes, automatic ISEE‑based allowance recalculation, selection and confirmation of allowance distribution between parents, ability to discard a draft and restart, presentation of a summary screen before submission, and notification of the application outcome. The current list also mixes many API‑centric implementations, which is acceptable, but the lack of correspondence to the defined high‑level goal and the omission of several key applicant actions reduce completeness and consistency.

[Applicant -> Consult Past Applications and History] The low‑level goals correctly map to the single high‑level goal and describe concrete functional actions the applicant can perform (listing applications, viewing details, seeing status history, filtering). They are all functional and pertain to the applicant actor. However, the set is somewhat incomplete: the description also mentions that applicants can download a receipt, view attached documents, and see payment information for past applications. Including low‑level goals such as “The system shall allow the applicant to download the receipt PDF for a submitted application” and “The system shall display any documents attached to a past application” would make the coverage more complete. Adding these would fully represent the functionality described.

[Other Parent -> Complete Shared Application] The low‑level goals are all functional and map clearly to actions that the “Other Parent” actor would perform when completing a shared AUU application. They cover retrieving the application, reviewing entered data, adjusting allowance distribution, providing payment details, accepting declarations, reviewing a summary, submitting, downloading the receipt, and checking status. The set is largely complete and consistent with the description. Minor issues are the slight redundancy between “Retrieve Shared Application Details” and “Display Initiated Application Data” (these could be merged into a single “View Application Details” action) and the absence of an explicit goal for uploading additional documents if the application is suspended (which may be required for the other parent). Addressing these would make the list fully comprehensive.

[Other Parent -> Manage Shared AUU Allowance Distribution and Payment] The low‑level goals are all functional and each maps to a single action that the “Other Parent” can perform on the system (viewing the proposed distribution, confirming it, modifying it, submitting the modification, entering payment details, and submitting those details). They are consistent with the associated high‑level goal and do not contain non‑functional requirements. The set is complete for the scoped high‑level goal, though a brief “Validate entered payment information” step could be added for completeness.

[INPS Staff -> Process and Decide on AUU Applications] The low‑level goals only cover actions performed by INPS staff (retrieving applications, viewing details, handling documents, adding notes, changing status, requesting docs, sending notifications). While these are functional and correctly mapped to the staff actor, they omit all functional goals for the primary users – the applicants/parents – who, according to the description, must be able to start, save, resume, and submit applications; enter child and family data; receive real‑time fiscal‑code validation; select payment methods; accept declarations and privacy notices; upload additional documents; add new children to an existing application; and consult past applications or simulate allowances. Because the low‑level goal set is not a complete representation of the system’s functionality, the model is significantly incomplete.

[INPS Staff -> Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE] The low‑level goal set is inconsistent with the provided high‑level goals and actors. Only one high‑level goal (automatic ISEE‑based allowance adjustment) is defined, yet the low‑level list contains many applicant‑centric actions (initiate application, save draft, add child, upload documents, confirm declarations, select payment method, submit, retrieve status, view adjustment details, update contact) that belong to a different high‑level goal (“Manage AUU Application and Personal Data”) which is missing from the high‑level specification. This mismatch violates the requirement that each low‑level goal map to a defined high‑level goal.

Furthermore, several low‑level goals are non‑functional or overly administrative (e.g., “Review Allowance Calculation Rules”, “Verify Applicant Notification Content”, “View Allowance Adjustment Audit Log”) and do not represent a single functional action performed by an actor. Important functional actions described in the system description are absent, such as:
- Real‑time fiscal‑code validation and duplicate detection.
- Blocking the flow when a child is already linked to another active application.
- Handling draft discard vs. resume.
- Supporting the other parent’s completion of an application and allowance distribution changes.
- Adding new children to an existing submitted application.
- Simulating allowance amounts and consulting general information.

To improve the model, add the missing high‑level goals (e.g., “Manage AUU Application Lifecycle”, “Support Multi‑Parent Collaboration”, “Provide Information and Simulation Services”) and ensure every low‑level goal is a functional, single‑step action tied to one of those goals. Remove non‑functional review or audit goals, and include the omitted functional actions listed above.

[INPS Staff -> Ensure Timely Allowance Disbursement] The low‑level goal set mixes system‑internal processes (e.g., “Identify Eligible Applications for Monthly Disbursement”, “Initiate Allowance Payment Transaction”, “Record Monthly Disbursement Status”) with actor‑centric actions, violating the rule that each low‑level goal should correspond to a single action performed by an actor through the software. Moreover, many goals are linked to high‑level goals that are not defined in the provided high‑level list (e.g., “Enable Applicants to Submit Complete AUU Applications”, “Support Application Evaluation and Decision”), creating inconsistency. Several essential applicant actions described in the specification are missing (e.g., viewing validation errors, downloading the receipt, cancelling or deleting a draft, confirming the final submission, reviewing the payment schedule). Some goals overlap or are too granular (e.g., separate “Select Payment Method” and “Confirm Payment Method”). To improve the model, restrict low‑level goals to functional, actor‑driven actions, ensure each is tied to an existing high‑level goal, add the missing applicant actions, and remove or re‑classify internal system tasks as non‑functional or separate technical requirements.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) cover the core workflow of submitting an AUU application, including initiation, data entry (applicant, children, payment), validation, legal acceptance, and final submission. However, several LLGs are clearly unrelated to the specific parent HLG 'Submit AUU Application' or belong to different functional intentions as defined in the project description:

1. **llg_022 (Add Child to Submitted Application)**: The project description states that adding children to an *existing* (submitted) application is a distinct supporting function/modification process, not part of the initial submission flow. It belongs to a 'Modify Application' or 'Manage Existing Application' HLG.
2. **llg_027 (Upload Post-Suspension Documents)** and **llg_028 (Reconfirm Suspended Application)**: These actions occur *after* submission and evaluation, specifically in response to a suspension. They belong to a 'Respond to Suspension' or 'Manage Application Status' HLG, not the initial submission.
3. **llg_029 (View Submitted Application History)**: The project description lists 'consult previously submitted applications' as a supporting function, distinct from the act of submitting a new one.
4. **llg_030 (Simulate AUU Allowance)**: The project description explicitly lists 'simulate the expected monthly allowance amount' as a supporting function, separate from the application submission process.
5. **llg_031 (Access AUU Benefit Information)**: The project description lists 'consult general information' as a supporting function, unrelated to the transactional act of submitting an application.

Additionally, **llg_011 (Invite Second Parent)** and **llg_025/026 (Accept/Complete Second Parent Section)** describe a collaborative workflow. While the project mentions the other parent can complete the application, the 'Submit AUU Application' HLG typically focuses on the primary applicant's submission action. However, since the project description says 'The system also allows an application originally submitted by one parent to be completed by the other parent', this is a distinct functional intention from the primary submission. But more critically, llg_022, 027, 028, 029, 030, and 031 are clearly outside the scope of 'Submit AUU Application'.

Given the presence of multiple LLGs that clearly belong to different functional intentions (post-submission management, simulation, information retrieval), the decomposition is misleading for the specific HLG 'Submit AUU Application'. A regeneration is required to focus strictly on the submission workflow.
evaluation.regeneration_feedback: The current LLGs include capabilities that belong to other HLGs such as 'Manage Existing Application' (llg_022), 'Respond to Suspension' (llg_027, llg_028), 'Consult Application History' (llg_029), 'Simulate Allowance' (llg_030), and 'Access General Information' (llg_031). Please regenerate the LLGs to strictly cover the workflow of creating, filling, validating, and submitting a *new* AUU application, excluding post-submission modifications, simulations, and general information retrieval.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Manage Application Drafts'. 
1. **llg_001 (Create)**: Aligns with 'save an incomplete application as a draft'.
2. **llg_002 (Update)**: Aligns with 'resume... or discard it' (implying the ability to continue editing/saving changes) and general draft management.
3. **llg_003 (Retrieve List)**: Necessary for the user to find their drafts to resume or discard them. The project description states 'A saved draft can later be consulted', implying the user needs a way to locate it.
4. **llg_004 (Load Specific)**: Necessary to 'resume' the draft. The description mentions resuming from saved info or restarting, which requires loading the specific draft state.
5. **llg_005 (Delete)**: Aligns with 'discard it'.

There are no duplicates, contradictions, or unrelated goals. The set covers the essential capabilities of creating, listing, loading, updating, and deleting drafts. No essential capabilities are missing for this specific HLG.

evaluation.rationale: The parent HLG is 'Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup'. LLGs llg_001 through llg_007 are directly related to selecting, configuring, validating, and finalizing payment methods (bank, postal, co-parent), which aligns with the HLG. However, LLGs llg_008 through llg_024 cover a wide range of unrelated functionalities such as initiating new applications, adding child/family data, validating fiscal codes, saving drafts, accepting declarations, submitting applications, downloading receipts, uploading documents, managing existing applications, viewing history, and simulating allowances. These LLGs belong to different functional intentions (e.g., 'Submit AUU Application', 'Manage Application Data', 'Consult Application History') and are unrelated to the specific goal of managing payment setup. Therefore, they are marked as unsupported/misleading for this specific HLG decomposition.
evaluation.regeneration_feedback: The current list of LLGs contains many goals unrelated to the parent HLG 'Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup'. Please regenerate the LLGs to focus exclusively on the selection, configuration, validation, and management of payment methods (e.g., bank transfer, postal order, prepaid card) and co-parent payment details. Remove LLGs related to application initiation, child data entry, draft management, declaration acceptance, application submission, document upload, history consultation, and allowance simulation.

branch_003.rationale: The parent HLG is 'Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup'. LLGs llg_001 through llg_007 are directly related to selecting, configuring, validating, and finalizing payment methods (bank, postal, co-parent), which aligns with the HLG. However, LLGs llg_008 through llg_024 cover a wide range of unrelated functionalities such as initiating new applications, adding child/family data, validating fiscal codes, saving drafts, accepting declarations, submitting applications, downloading receipts, uploading documents, managing existing applications, viewing history, and simulating allowances. evaluation.rationale: The parent HLG is 'Monitor Application Status', which focuses on tracking the progress and outcome of submitted applications. Several LLGs (llg_007 through llg_021, llg_024 through llg_026) describe actions related to creating, editing, submitting, or managing application data (e.g., initiating new applications, updating child data, selecting payment methods, accepting declarations, submitting the application, or managing co-parent distributions). These actions belong to the functional intention of 'Managing/Creating Applications' or 'Completing Applications', not 'Monitoring Status'. While 'ConsultPreviousApplicationDetails' (llg_006) and 'UploadSupportingDocument' (llg_013) are borderline, the former is a read-only retrieval consistent with monitoring/consultation, and the latter is a specific action required to resolve a 'Suspended' status, which is part of the monitoring/resolution loop. However, the bulk of the list (llg_007-llg_012, llg_014-llg_021, llg_024-llg_026) clearly belongs to a different functional intention (Application Creation/Management). Therefore, the decomposition is misleading as it mixes distinct functional intentions. The core monitoring capabilities (llg_001-llg_005) are valid. The presence of unrelated LLGs necessitates regeneration to isolate the correct scope for this HLG.
evaluation.regeneration_feedback: The current list of Low-Level Goals contains many goals that belong to the 'Create/Manage Application' functional intention rather than 'Monitor Application Status'. Please regenerate the LLGs to strictly focus on tracking, viewing status, viewing outcomes, and handling notifications for *already submitted* applications. Remove goals related to initiating new applications, editing application data (child info, payment, declarations), submitting applications, downloading receipts (unless specifically tied to status confirmation, but usually part of submission), simulating amounts, or managing co-parent distributions. Keep only goals that allow the applicant to observe the state of existing applications.

evaluation.rationale:
The provided Low-Level Goals (LLGs) accurately decompose the High-Level Goal 'Respond to Documentation Requests'. 
1. llg_001 (Retrieve list) is necessary for the applicant to identify which applications are suspended.
2. llg_002 (Retrieve details) is essential to know what documents are required and what data needs reconfirmation, as specified in the project description ('INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required').
3. llg_003 (Upload document) directly addresses the core requirement to 'upload the requested attachments'.
4. llg_004 (Update data fields) addresses the requirement to 'reconfirm the application data'.
5. llg_005 (Resubmit) addresses the final step of the process, allowing the application to be evaluated again after the applicant has 'reconfirm the application data' and accepted declarations (implied by the resubmission action in this context, or handled by a separate declaration acceptance LLG if strictly separated, but resubmission is the functional trigger for the state change). 

There are no duplicates, contradictions, or unrelated goals. The granularity is appropriate for API-level requirements. No essential capabilities are missing for the specific scope of responding to a suspension.

No essential capabilities are missing for the specific scope of 'receiving the receipt' (e.g., email notification is not explicitly required by the HLG description, which focuses on the downloadable artifact). The granularity is acceptable for a low-level decomposition.

Therefore, the branch should be regenerated to focus only on the relevant validation steps.

evaluation.rationale:
The parent HLG 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE' describes a system-driven process where the allowance is recalculated automatically when ISEE data becomes available, explicitly stating 'without requiring applicant intervention'. The actor is 'INPS Staff'. 

1. **LLGs llg_001 to llg_007**: These describe actions performed by INPS Staff (reviewing status, reviewing results, manual triggers, approval, audit logs, rules, notifications). While the HLG emphasizes 'automatic' adjustment, INPS Staff often needs to monitor, verify, or intervene in such systems. These are relevant to the management and oversight of the ISEE-based adjustment process. They are not clearly unrelated or duplicated. 

2. **LLGs llg_008 to llg_017**: These describe actions performed by the 'Applicant' (Initiate Application, Save Draft, Add Child, Upload Document, Confirm Declarations, Specify Payment, Submit Application, Retrieve Status, View Details, Update Contact). 
   - The actor for the parent HLG is 'INPS Staff'. 
   - The descriptions of these LLGs explicitly state 'Applicant sends a request...'. 
   - These actions belong to the 'Application Submission' or 'Applicant Management' functional intentions, not the 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE' intention. 
   - Specifically, llg_008 (Initiate New AUU Application) is the start of the application process, not the ISEE adjustment. 
   - llg_016 (View Allowance Adjustment Details) is performed by the Applicant, whereas llg_005 (View Allowance Adjustment Audit Log) is performed by INPS Staff. While related to the same data, they serve different actors and functional contexts (citizen service vs. staff administration). However, the primary issue is that llg_008-llg_015 and llg_017 are clearly unrelated to the specific HLG of *adjusting* the allowance based on ISEE. They are part of the general application lifecycle. 
   - The prompt states: 'Mark an LLG as unsupported or misleading only when it is ... unrelated to the parent HLG, or belongs to a different functional intention.' 
   - llg_008 through llg_015 and llg_017 belong to the 'Manage AUU Application' or 'Submit AUU Application' functional intention, not 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE'. Therefore, they are unrelated to the parent HLG. 
   - llg_016 is borderline. It is about viewing adjustment details. However, it is assigned to the Applicant. The HLG is about the system adjusting the allowance. The applicant viewing it is a consequence, but the core HLG is about the adjustment mechanism. Given the strict instruction to mark unrelated LLGs, and that the actor in the HLG is INPS Staff, LLGs describing Applicant actions are generally considered to belong to a different actor's goal tree. However, the prompt says 'Evaluate only the supplied actor and parent HLG'. The supplied actor is INPS Staff. The LLGs llg_008-llg_017 describe Applicant actions. Thus, they are not actions of the supplied actor. They are unrelated to the INPS Staff's goal of managing the ISEE adjustment. 

Therefore, llg_008 through llg_017 are unsupported/misleading because they describe actions by a different actor (Applicant) and belong to a different functional intention (Application Submission/Management) than the parent HLG (ISEE-based Allowance Adjustment by Staff).

This requires a regeneration of the LLGs to focus strictly on the disbursement workflow (identifying eligible approved apps, calculating amounts if dynamic, initiating payment, recording status, handling expiration).

This includes initial application creation, entering personal and child details, verifying information, attaching documents, specifying payment methods, collaborating with a second parent, saving drafts, reviewing, and finally submitting the application and receiving confirmation.

These operations cover the entire lifecycle of an application draft, from its initial creation to its eventual removal, all centered around the applicant's ability to control their progress on an application.

branch_003.rationale: The low-level goals collectively describe the complete process an applicant (and potentially a co-parent) undertakes to set up, modify, view, and finalize the method and specific details by which they will receive the AUU allowance. replacement_request.rationale: The original HLG 'Submit AUU Application' is too narrow, focusing only on the final act of submission. The project description details a complex multi-phase process involving the creation, population, validation, and management of application data (including child details, ISEE context, payment methods, and declarations) prior to submission. The scope must be broadened to 'Apply for' the benefit to encompass the entire lifecycle of preparing and managing the application data, not just the final transmission.
replacement_request.generation_project_description:
The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU), a financial benefit provided by INPS to families with dependent children. The considered scenario focuses exclusively on applications submitted directly by interested users through the INPS website, excluding applications submitted by delegated patronage institutions, mobile applications, and call-center interactions.

An authenticated applicant can apply for an AUU benefit as a parent, foster parent, or legal guardian of a child. During the first phase of the application, the applicant provides information about each dependent child, including the child's fiscal code, dependency status, disability status and, when applicable, disability level. Depending on the applicant type, additional information concerning family composition, exclusive custody, the other parent's fiscal code, and the requested allowance distribution between parents must also be provided.

When a child's fiscal code is entered, the system verifies it in real time. If the child is already associated with another active application, the application flow is blocked and an explanatory warning is shown. The applicant may also specify adult dependent children who do not directly qualify for AUU but contribute to determining household composition. Duplicate fiscal codes for adult children are detected and reported.

The amount of the allowance depends on the applicant's economic situation. If INPS does not already possess a valid ISEE when the application is submitted, the minimum allowance established by regulation is used. If a valid ISEE becomes available later, INPS automatically recalculates the allowance without requiring the applicant to modify the application.

In the payment phase, the applicant specifies the payment method. If the allowance is to be divided equally between both parents, the payment information of the other parent must also be provided. Supported payment methods include credit to a SEPA IBAN account owned by the beneficiary, domiciled payment at a post office, and credit to an eligible prepaid card.

Before submitting the application, the applicant must read and accept the declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice. The system then presents a summary of the entered information so that it can be reviewed. If validation errors are detected, the application is not submitted and the applicant must correct the erroneous information. If validation succeeds, the application is submitted and a receipt can be downloaded.

An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed. When resuming a draft, the applicant may either continue from the previously saved information or discard it and restart the application from the beginning.

Once submitted, the application is evaluated by authorized INPS staff. The application may be accepted, rejected because the applicant is not entitled to the benefit, or suspended when additional documentation is required. The applicant is notified of the outcome. An accepted application remains valid for twelve months and the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every month.

When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required. The applicant can consult the application, upload the requested attachments, reconfirm the application data, and again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice.

The system also allows an application originally submitted by one parent to be completed by the other parent. The other parent can consult the application and confirm or modify the proposed allowance distribution. If the applicant requested the entire allowance, the other parent may accept the 100 percent allocation or request a 50 percent distribution. When payment to the other parent is required, that parent provides their own payment information.

Applicants can also add one or more children to an existing application. Each new child's fiscal code is checked in real time to ensure that the child is not already associated with another active application. After adding the child, existing payment and declaration data can be confirmed or modified.

Finally, the system provides supporting functions that allow citizens to consult previously submitted applications, consult general information about the Assegno Unico Universale, and simulate the expected monthly allowance amount.

branch_002.rationale: The project description explicitly supports the functionality of saving an application as a draft, consulting it later, and either continuing or discarding it. The original High-Level Goal 'Manage Application Drafts' accurately captures this functional intention for the Applicant actor. It is distinct from 'Submit AUU Application' (which focuses on the final submission) and 'Consult Past Applications' (which focuses on submitted history). The scope is appropriate and the description is faithful to the requirements. The parent HLG 'Manage Application Drafts' requires the ability to save, resume, or discard incomplete applications. The documentation states: 'An application may be interrupted without saving or saved as a draft before submission. A saved draft can later be consulted and completed. When resuming a draft, the applicant may either continue from the previously saved information or discard it and restart the application from the beginning.' The current LLGs cover: 1) Creating a draft (saving state), 2) Updating a draft (modifying/saving changes), 3) Listing drafts (retrieving list), 4) Loading a specific draft (retrieving details to resume), and 5) Deleting a draft (removing/discarding). These five LLGs collectively cover the full lifecycle of a draft: creation, modification, retrieval (list and detail), and deletion. The capability to 'resume' is effectively covered by 'Load Specific Application Draft' (llg_004) which enables the applicant to access the data to continue editing, and 'Update Application Draft' (llg_002) which allows saving the continued progress. The capability to 'discard' is covered by 'Delete Application Draft' (llg_005). There are no missing essential capabilities explicitly required by the parent HLG that are absent from the current LLGs. The decomposition is complete and consistent with the documentation.

The bottom-up reconstruction 'Configure AUU Allowance Payment Information' is semantically equivalent but slightly more precise in describing the action of setting up the details. Therefore, the original goal is kept as it is faithful and reasonably scoped.

high_level_evaluation.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Monitor Application Status' is supported by the project description, which states that applicants can consult applications and are notified of outcomes. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Applicants to Monitor and Manage Submitted Applications' suggests a broader scope that includes management actions. Looking at the other existing High-Level Goals, specific management actions are already covered by distinct goals: 'Respond to Documentation Requests', 'Modify Existing Application', and 'Complete Shared Application'. The 'Monitor' aspect is partially covered by 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' (notifications) and 'Consult Past Applications and History' (viewing details). The original goal 'Monitor Application Status' specifically targets tracking progress and outcome. While 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' covers the notification aspect, 'Monitor Application Status' implies the active ability to check the current state (e.g., via a dashboard or status view) which is distinct from just receiving a notification or viewing historical records. However, 'Consult Past Applications and History' explicitly mentions accessing and reviewing previously submitted applications including their complete history and details. This overlaps significantly with monitoring status. Furthermore, 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' covers the outcome aspect. The original goal is somewhat redundant with 'Consult Past Applications and History' (which allows checking status) and 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' (which informs of the status change). The reconstruction 'Monitor and Manage' is too broad because 'Manage' is already split into specific HLGs. The original 'Monitor Application Status' is a valid, distinct functional intention (checking current status) that is not fully captured by 'Be Informed' (passive notification) or 'Consult Past' (historical review, though it includes current). However, 'Consult Past Applications and History' is described as 'access and review all previously submitted AUU applications, including their complete history and details'. This effectively covers monitoring the status of any submitted application. Therefore, the original goal is largely subsumed by 'Consult Past Applications and History' and 'Be Informed of Application Outcome'. Keeping a separate 'Monitor Application Status' goal creates semantic overlap. It is better to remove it to avoid redundancy, as the ability to check status is inherent in consulting the application details and receiving notifications.

branch_015.rationale:

The description explicitly mentions that when suspended, 'the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required'. The original goal is appropriately scoped for the INPS Staff actor, distinguishing it from the Applicant's goals (like 'Respond to Documentation Requests' or 'Be Informed of Application Outcome'). It does not overlap with the other INPS Staff goals ('Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE' and 'Ensure Timely Allowance Disbursement'), which focus on post-decision administrative/automated processes rather than the initial evaluation and decision-making phase. Therefore, the original goal should be kept. 1. **Retrieval**: LLG_001 (List) and LLG_002 (Details) allow staff to find and inspect applications. LLG_003 allows access to attached documents, which is critical for evaluation.

The descriptions for Reject and Suspend include providing a reason, which aligns with the documentation stating that suspension requires specifying additional documents and rejection implies a lack of entitlement (reasoning is standard practice and implied by 'make a decision').
4. **Documentation Requests**: LLG_008 explicitly covers the capability to 'request additional documentation when necessary', which is a specific requirement in the HLG description and project documentation ('When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required').
5. **Notification**: LLG_009 covers sending notifications to the applicant. While the sibling HLG 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' exists for the applicant's perspective, the action of *sending* the notification is an operational task performed by the system/staff as part of the decision process. The documentation states 'The applicant is notified of the outcome', implying a system action triggered by the staff decision. Including this as an LLG for the staff/system actor is appropriate to ensure the decision is communicated.

1. **Retrieval**: LLG_001 (List) and LLG_002 (Details) allow staff to find and inspect applications. LLG_003 allows access to attached documents, which is critical for evaluation.
2. **Evaluation/Notes**: LLG_004 allows adding internal notes, supporting the 'review and evaluate' aspect.
3. **Decision Making**: LLG_005, LLG_006, and LLG_007 explicitly cover the three decision outcomes: Accept, Reject, and Suspend. The descriptions for Reject and Suspend include providing a reason, which aligns with the documentation stating that suspension requires specifying additional documents and rejection implies a lack of entitlement (reasoning is standard practice and implied by 'make a decision').
4. **Documentation Requests**: LLG_008 explicitly covers the capability to 'request additional documentation when necessary', which is a specific requirement in the HLG description and project documentation ('When an application is suspended, the INPS operator specifies which additional documents are required').
5. **Notification**: LLG_009 covers sending notifications to the applicant. While the sibling HLG 'Be Informed of Application Outcome' exists for the applicant's perspective, the action of *sending* the notification is an operational task performed by the system/staff as part of the decision process. The documentation states 'The applicant is notified of the outcome', implying a system action triggered by the staff decision. Including this as an LLG for the staff/system actor is appropriate to ensure the decision is communicated.

No essential capabilities are missing. The capabilities owned by sibling HLGs (like automatic ISEE adjustment or disbursement) are correctly excluded. The decomposition is atomic and API-mappable. There are no contradictions with the documentation.

branch_016.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE' is supported by the project description, which states that if a valid ISEE becomes available later, INPS automatically recalculates the allowance. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Manage AUU Allowance Adjustments for Applicants' suggests a broader scope that includes monitoring, triggering, reviewing, and auditing these adjustments. The original goal is somewhat narrow, focusing only on the automatic recalculation aspect, whereas the reconstructed goal encompasses the full management cycle of allowance adjustments by INPS staff. Given that the project description emphasizes the automatic nature of the recalculation without requiring applicant intervention, and considering the role of INPS staff in overseeing this process, the original goal is reasonably scoped but could be slightly broadened to align with the comprehensive management aspect implied by the reconstruction. However, since the core intention (automatic adjustment based on ISEE) is clearly supported and distinct from other HLGs, it is appropriate to keep the original goal with minor adjustments to reflect the management aspect if necessary. In this case, the original goal is sufficiently specific and supported, so it should be kept. The current Low-Level Goals (LLGs) comprehensively cover the essential activities required by the parent High-Level Goal (HLG) 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE'. The HLG focuses on the automatic recalculation and update of the AUU allowance when a valid ISEE becomes available, without applicant intervention. The LLGs address: 1) Monitoring the ISEE data ingestion (llg_001), 2) Reviewing the automatic recalculation results (llg_002), 3) Providing a manual override/trigger capability (llg_003) which is a standard operational control for such systems, 4) Approving the final update to the record (llg_004), 5) Auditing the changes (llg_005), 6) Understanding the calculation rules (llg_006), and 7) Verifying notifications to the applicant (llg_007). These goals align with the actor 'INPS Staff' and the system's behavior described in the documentation (automatic recalculation, no applicant intervention required). There are no contradictions with the documentation, and no essential capabilities explicitly required by the HLG are missing. The sibling HLGs do not overlap with these specific adjustment/audit tasks.

branch_017.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Ensure Timely Allowance Disbursement' is supported by the project description, which states that 'the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every month' for accepted applications. However, the bottom-up reconstruction 'Process Monthly Allowance Disbursements for Approved Applications' is more precise and faithful to the system's functional scope. The original goal uses the verb 'Ensure', which implies a quality attribute or a broader responsibility that might overlap with system reliability or the applicant's goal of receiving funds. The reconstructed goal focuses on the specific functional process of handling the disbursement for approved applications, which aligns better with the low-level goals describing the identification, validation, and execution of payments. Additionally, the actor 'INPS Staff' is responsible for the evaluation, but the disbursement is described as an automatic system process. While the staff initiates the approval, the 'Process' framing is more accurate for the system's operational goal than 'Ensure'. Therefore, rewriting to match the more precise functional intention is appropriate.

replacement_request.rationale: The original goal focused on the assurance of 'timeliness,' which is a non-functional quality attribute. The refined goal shifts focus to the functional processing of monthly disbursements for approved applications, aligning with the system's automated payment workflow described in the project context. The actor remains INPS Staff, as they are the authorized personnel responsible for the evaluation and management of the application lifecycle that triggers these disbursements.
replacement_request.generation_project_description: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU). Once an application is submitted and evaluated by authorized INPS staff, it may be accepted. An accepted application remains valid for twelve months, and the corresponding allowance is paid automatically every month. The system handles the functional processing of these monthly disbursements for approved applications, ensuring that the financial benefit is transferred to the designated beneficiaries according to the specified payment methods (SEPA IBAN, post office, or prepaid card) for the duration of the application's validity.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description's functional intentions are fully covered by the existing High-Level Goals. The core workflow of submitting an application is covered by 'Submit AUU Application'. The specific steps of validating child data ('Ensure Valid Child Data Submission'), accepting legal terms ('Accept Legal Declarations'), and receiving confirmation ('Receive Application Receipt') are all present. The management of incomplete applications is covered by 'Manage Application Drafts'. The post-submission lifecycle, including tracking status ('Monitor Application Status'), receiving notifications ('Be Informed of Application Outcome'), and handling suspensions ('Respond to Documentation Requests'), is comprehensively addressed. The ability to update active applications is covered by 'Modify Existing Application'. The collaborative aspect involving the second parent is covered by 'Complete Shared Application' and 'Manage Shared AUU Allowance Distribution and Payment'. Finally, the informational and administrative functions (consulting history, general info, simulation) are covered by 'Consult Past Applications and History' and 'Access Benefit Information'. The INPS staff goals cover the evaluation, decision-making, and automatic administrative processes (ISEE adjustment, disbursement). No distinct, documented functional intention remains uncovered.

branch_001.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Apply for AUU Benefit' is supported by the project description, which details the process of initiating, completing, and submitting an application. However, the original description explicitly includes 'the ability to save and resume applications as drafts'. Looking at the 'Other current High-Level Goals', there is a distinct goal named 'Manage Application Drafts' which covers this specific functionality. Including draft management in the 'Apply for AUU Benefit' goal creates semantic overlap and incorrect scoping, as draft management is a separate functional intention (managing the state of the application before final submission) rather than the core act of applying itself. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Complete and submit an Assegno Unico Universale benefit application' correctly isolates the core application submission process, excluding the draft management aspect which is already covered by another HLG. Therefore, the original goal should be rewritten to remove the reference to drafts and align with the core submission intention.

According to the evaluator's instructions, this functionality is covered by a separate 'Manage Application Drafts' goal and must be removed to keep the current goal focused strictly on the initiation, completion, and submission of the application. replacement_request.generation_project_description: The system supports the online management of applications for the Italian Assegno Unico Universale (AUU). This specific scenario focuses exclusively on the end-to-end process of an authenticated applicant initiating, completing, and submitting a new application for the benefit. The applicant acts as a parent, foster parent, or legal guardian. The process involves providing information about dependent children (fiscal code, dependency, disability status) and, depending on the applicant type, family composition and custody details. The system performs real-time validation of fiscal codes to prevent conflicts with other active applications. The applicant specifies payment methods (SEPA IBAN, post office, or prepaid card) and, if applicable, provides payment details for the other parent if the allowance is to be shared. Before final submission, the applicant must review a summary of the entered information, accept the declarations of responsibility and GDPR privacy notice, and pass system validation. If validation fails, the applicant must correct errors; if successful, the application is submitted and a receipt is generated. This goal excludes the management of saved drafts, the evaluation of submitted applications by INPS staff, the handling of suspended applications, and the modification of existing applications.

branch_003.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup' is supported by the project description, which details the applicant's need to specify payment methods (SEPA IBAN, post office, prepaid card) and provide associated details. However, the term 'Manage' is slightly broader than the specific action of configuring or specifying payment details during the application process. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Configure AUU Allowance Payment Information' is more precise and aligns better with the functional intent of setting up the payment method and details. Additionally, the existing HLG 'Apply for AUU Benefit' already includes 'providing all necessary family, child, and payment information', which creates some overlap. However, since payment setup is a distinct and significant part of the application process, especially when involving co-parents or specific payment methods, it is reasonable to keep a dedicated HLG for it. branch_005.rationale: The original High-Level Goal 'Respond to Documentation Requests' is supported by the project description, which explicitly states that when an application is suspended, the applicant can consult it, upload requested attachments, reconfirm data, and accept declarations. The bottom-up reconstruction 'Enable Applicants to Resolve Suspended Applications' captures the same functional intention but frames it as the broader outcome (resolving the suspension) rather than the specific action (responding to requests). However, the original goal is reasonably scoped and accurately reflects the applicant's specific task in this workflow. It does not overlap significantly with 'Monitor Application Status' (which is about tracking) or 'Modify Existing Application' (which typically refers to active applications, not suspended ones requiring specific documentation). The original goal is a distinct and necessary step in the lifecycle of a suspended application. Therefore, it should be kept. The current low-level goals (LLGs) cover the core workflow for responding to a suspended application: identifying suspended applications (llg_001), understanding the specific requirements (llg_002), uploading documents (llg_003), updating data (llg_004), and resubmitting (llg_005). However, the project description explicitly states that when an application is suspended, the applicant must 'again accept the responsibility declarations and privacy notice' before resubmitting. This is a distinct, mandatory step in the resubmission workflow. While there is a sibling HLG 'Accept Legal Declarations', it is described in the context of 'application submission' (initial). The suspension workflow requires a *re-acceptance* as part of the specific 'Respond to Documentation Requests' flow to validate the updated data. The current LLGs do not include a step to re-accept these declarations. Without this, the resubmission (llg_005) would be incomplete or invalid according to the documented business rules. Therefore, a capability to re-accept declarations is missing from this specific branch.

missing_hlg_evaluation.rationale: The project description's functional intentions are fully covered by the existing High-Level Goals. The core application workflow is covered by 'Apply for AUU Benefit'. Draft management is covered by 'Manage Application Drafts'. Payment setup is covered by 'Manage AUU Allowance Payment Setup'. Status tracking and notifications are covered by 'Monitor Application Status' and 'Be Informed of Application Outcome'. Handling suspended applications is covered by 'Respond to Documentation Requests'. Adding children to existing applications is covered by 'Modify Existing Application'. General information and simulation are covered by 'Access Benefit Information'. Legal declarations are covered by 'Accept Legal Declarations'. Receipts are covered by 'Receive Application Receipt'. Data validation is covered by 'Ensure Valid Child Data Submission'. History consultation is covered by 'Consult Past Applications and History'. The 'Other Parent' actor's specific actions (completing the application, managing distribution/payment) are covered by 'Complete Shared Application' and 'Manage Shared AUU Allowance Distribution and Payment'. The 'INPS Staff' actor's actions (processing decisions, ISEE recalculation, disbursement) are covered by 'Process and Decide on AUU Applications', 'Automatically Adjust Allowance Based on ISEE', and 'Ensure Timely Allowance Disbursement'. No distinct, undocumented functional intention remains uncovered.

This includes initiating the application, providing all necessary personal, dependent, household, financial, and payment details, performing validation checks, agreeing to legal terms, and finally sending the application for official processing. All these actions are sequential or interdependent steps required to achieve the successful submission of a single AUU application.
